click.rationale: `Clicks on the provided element` can activate page UI, including attacker-controlled controls or submissions, so it can be a SINK. If `includeSnapshot` is used, the response includes a page snapshot; page content can be private user/SaaS/intranet data or attacker-authored web content. Snapshot `uid` values identify elements for later calls.

close_page.rationale: `Closes the page by its index`; this changes browser state but does not advertise returning data or sending agent-supplied content to an attacker-readable destination.

drag.rationale: `Drag an element onto another element` can trigger page-side state changes or submissions, so it can be a SINK. If `includeSnapshot` is used, returned page snapshot text may be private or attacker-authored; snapshot `uid` values are identifiers for later calls.

emulate.rationale: The tool `Emulates various features on the target page`; in particular `extraHttpHeaders` are `included into every HTTP request originating from the page and persist across navigations`, so agent-supplied header values can be sent to web hosts.

evaluate_script.rationale: `Evaluate a JavaScript function inside the target page` and examples include `await fetch("example.com")`; page JS can read private page state and return it, fetch attacker-controlled content and return it, or send data to arbitrary hosts. This is page-context execution, not host code execution, so it is not HOSTEXEC. `filePath` can write returned output to a local file.

fill.rationale: `Type text into an input` sends the `value` into the target page, where attacker-controlled page scripts can read or submit it. If `includeSnapshot` is used, the returned snapshot may contain private or attacker-authored page text and element `uid` identifiers.

fill_form.rationale: `Fill out multiple form elements` sends `value` data into page form fields, which attacker-controlled page scripts can read or submit. If `includeSnapshot` is used, the returned snapshot may contain private or attacker-authored text and `uid` identifiers.

get_console_message.rationale: `Gets a console message`; console messages on a logged-in or local page may contain non-public data, and attacker-controlled pages can author console text. `msgid` identifies a message selected from `list_console_messages`.

get_network_request.rationale: It gets a network request and is `Useful for inspecting request headers (including 'Cookie') and response headers`; cookies and bodies can be non-public, while response bodies/headers/URLs can be attacker-controlled. Optional file paths can save request or response bodies locally.

handle_dialog.rationale: `handle`ing a browser dialog can enter `promptText` into a page prompt; an attacker-controlled page can read the prompt response, so this can send agent-supplied data to the page.

hover.rationale: `Hover over the provided element` changes page interaction state and can trigger page scripts or requests. If `includeSnapshot` is used, returned page snapshot text can be private or attacker-authored, with `uid` identifiers for later calls.

lighthouse_audit.rationale: `Get Lighthouse score and reports` for the target page; reports for logged-in, local, or intranet pages may include private page-derived details, and reports for attacker-controlled pages can include attacker-controlled page-derived text/URLs. `outputDirPath` writes reports locally.

list_console_messages.rationale: `List all console messages for the target page`; console output on private pages may include secrets, and attacker-controlled pages can author console messages. Listed message IDs can be used with `get_console_message`.

list_network_requests.rationale: `Lists the most recent requests for the target page`; request URLs and metadata for logged-in/local pages can be non-public, and attacker-controlled pages can generate attacker-controlled request URLs. Returned request IDs can be used by `get_network_request`.

list_pages.rationale: `Get a list of pages open in the browser`; open page URLs/titles can reveal non-public browsing/account state, and attacker-controlled pages can choose page titles/URLs. The exact returned fields are not advertised, so this keeps the conservative labels.

navigate_page.rationale: `Go to a URL, or back, forward, or reload`; with `type=url`, the `url` is an agent-chosen network destination, and `initScript` is agent-supplied script executed on the next document, so the tool can send data to web hosts or page context.

new_page.rationale: `Open a new tab and load a URL`; the required `url` is an agent-chosen network destination, so data placed in the URL can be delivered to an attacker-controlled host. The new page ID is an identifier for later calls.

performance_analyze_insight.rationale: It `Provides more detailed information` on a performance insight from a trace recording. Trace-derived details for private pages may expose non-public URLs/content, and attacker pages can influence trace-derived names/URLs/text.

performance_start_trace.rationale: `Start a performance trace on the target webpage`; trace results and insight sets are derived from the page and network activity, which can include private page data or attacker-controlled URLs/text. `filePath` can save raw trace data locally, and `reload` can change page state.

performance_stop_trace.rationale: `Stop the active performance trace recording`; returned or saved trace results are page-derived and can contain private page/network details or attacker-controlled URLs/text. `filePath` can save raw trace data locally.

press_key.rationale: `Press a key or key combination` sends keystrokes to the page, where attacker-controlled pages can observe effects or trigger submissions. If `includeSnapshot` is used, returned page snapshot text may be private or attacker-authored and includes `uid` identifiers.

resize_page.rationale: `Resizes the page's window`; this changes browser/page state but does not advertise returning page content or sending agent-supplied content to a remote destination.

select_page.rationale: `Select a page as a context for future tool calls`; this selects/focuses an existing page but does not advertise returning private/untrusted page content or sending data out.

take_heapsnapshot.rationale: `Capture a heap snapshot of the target page` to a required local `filePath`. The advertised text says it saves to a local file, not that it returns the heap into the agent context or sends it to an attacker-readable destination.

take_screenshot.rationale: `Take a screenshot of the page or element`; screenshots can contain private logged-in/local page content or attacker-controlled page content. `filePath` can save the screenshot locally instead of returning it.

take_snapshot.rationale: `Take a text snapshot of the target page based on the a11y tree`; page text can be private or attacker-authored. The snapshot `lists page elements along with a unique identifier (uid)`, and `filePath` can save it locally.

type_text.rationale: `Type text using keyboard into a previously focused input`; agent-supplied `text` and optional `submitKey` go into the target page, where an attacker-controlled page can read or submit them.

upload_file.rationale: `Upload a file through a provided element`; local `filePaths` are sent to the selected page element, which can be attacker-controlled, so this is a SINK. If `includeSnapshot` is used, returned snapshot text may be private or attacker-authored and includes `uid` identifiers.

wait_for.rationale: `Wait for the specified text to appear on the selected page`; success/failure can reveal whether private text is present on a logged-in/local page. The exact response fields are not advertised, so output text injectability is left empty and the judgement is conservative.

value_conditions.effect: Controls availability of evaluate_script; the advertised annotations name condition `javascriptEvaluation`, but do not state that it is disabled by default.

notes: HOSTEXEC is not assigned: the advertised JavaScript execution is `inside the target page`, which is browser/page-context execution rather than arbitrary host code execution.
For browser interaction tools, `pageId`/element UIDs are treated as destinations when they determine which browser page or element is changed or receives input.
